title: Monday morning ride and knee
summary: Wren checked the weather for her commute by bike: dry until mid-afternoon with showers after four. She said her left knee was stiff, set a 12:30 reminder for physio exercises, confirmed Biscuit's flea treatment is due on Thursday the 5th and went over the calendar: a Lowmoor stand-up at 9:30 and a one-to-one with Priya.

title: Book club picks The Salt Road
summary: Wren's book club, Second Tuesday Readers, chose The Salt Road by Hester Vane, which she had suggested. At about 48 pages a day she can finish before the meeting on Tuesday 10 March at the Quay Street library. It will be book eight of her thirty for the year; the previous one, Winter Harbour, disappointed her.

title: Roughness sweeps for the flood model
summary: Wren asked how to test the Lowmoor flood model's sensitivity to Manning's n. The plan: a five-step sweep from 0.025 to 0.06 for the channel, a separate sweep for the floodplain, one chart per sweep for Priya's Thursday slide, a caveat for the Ashby gauge gap in November 2023, and asking Felix for drone imagery.

title: Portuguese vocabulary practice
summary: Wren practised twenty Portuguese words with example sentences, including rio, ponte, chuva, barco, ilha, farol, mercado, padaria, bilhete, praia, ontem, esquerda, direita, obrigada, peixe, vento, amigo, livro, janela and cozinha.

title: Knee rehab check-in
summary: Wren's knee was sore after a ride. MIST repeated Oskar's rehab plan (step-downs, wall sits, glute bridges, no downhill running until April), suggested doing the exercises when warm, advised checking the Corvid's saddle height, confirmed the next appointment on 18 March at 8:15 and logged pain at 4 out of 10.

title: Baking the focaccia
summary: Wren baked her overnight focaccia step by step: warming the cold-fermented dough, oiling the tin, stretching it to the corners, a 45-minute rise, dimpling, rosemary and flaky salt with no olives, and 22 minutes at 230 degrees until golden, then cooling on a rack.

title: Making red lentil soup
summary: Wren made red lentil soup: onion and carrot softened, garlic, cumin and smoked paprika, rinsed red lentils and 1.2 litres of stock simmered for 25 minutes, half blended, finished with lemon and salt, and a yoghurt garnish. It made about six bowls.

title: Freezing leftovers and noting the bake
summary: Wren asked about freezing: the soup keeps three months frozen and the focaccia a month. Jonah called it her best focaccia yet, so MIST added the method to her focaccia note: 18-hour ferment, 45-minute rise, 22 minutes at 230 degrees.

title: Varrow trip: plan, ferry, stays, birds and cost
summary: Wren turned friends' notes on the Isle of Varrow into a seven-day plan for 8 to 14 August with Jonah. MIST compared the overnight and day ferries from Fenwick pier, recommending the overnight sailing with a window cabin, picked the Net Loft in Merrow village from the guesthouse shortlist, listed seabirds, divers and seals by site, and costed the trip at about 1,530 pounds for two.
open_threads: book the ferry and the Net Loft in April

title: Varrow trip: rain plans, packing, knee and final plan
summary: MIST gave a rainy-day plan B for every Varrow day, wrote a packing list with layers, midge nets and walking poles, reworked the walking days around Wren's knee with the Tarn path as the longest at 11 km, then saved the final itinerary to her trip note with the April bookings: overnight ferry, Net Loft, lighthouse tour and Hollow Bay boat trip.

title: Planning Imogen's visit
summary: Wren planned her sister Imogen's stay from 21 to 23 March: a Saturday run on the coast path with Wren cycling alongside, a dark chocolate tart at Little Owl Coffee, a small gift for Imogen's new library job in May, and a Sunday visit to their mother Ada with lilies.
open_threads: buy a congratulations gift for Imogen

title: Friday morning routine
summary: Wren switched the kitchen lights on and off, checked the temperature, set an egg timer, checked for rain before walking Biscuit, played and paused the news, and set a reminder to buy oat milk on the way home.

title: Marrow Creek job offer
summary: Wren was offered the senior hydrologist job at Marrow Creek Water Board. She weighed about 15 percent more pay, hybrid work and more strategic catchment planning against a forty-minute commute by bike and leaving the Lowmoor team. The answer is due by Friday 13 March, with a start on 6 April; MIST saved a pros and cons note.

title: Allotment planting plan
summary: Wren planned plot 14, which she gets on 1 April: sowing times and spacing for broad beans, potatoes, onion sets, carrots, beetroot, runner beans and courgettes, then salad leaves and chard, a compost bin, a water butt and a raised bed Jonah could build. MIST saved it as her allotment plan.
open_threads: collect the plot keys on 1 April

title: Climbing at Granite Loft
summary: Wren climbed for two hours at Granite Loft with Mei and sent her first 6a since the knee injury, skipping drop-knee moves. MIST logged the send. Mei is on night shifts next week, so they will climb again after the 16th.
open_threads: message Mei about climbing on the 16th

title: Painting the spare room
summary: Wren decided to paint the spare room, her new study, in Hollow Fern, a sage green. One 5 litre tin covers two coats; no primer is needed over sound magnolia, just sugar soap and a light sand. Rafael said Ostrander Hardware can mix the paint.

title: Sunday batch cooking
summary: Wren planned the week's lunches: lentil soup from the freezer, a chickpea and spinach stew without chilli for Jonah, and a farro salad with squash and feta. She added coffee to the shopping list and set a reminder for the Sunday call with her mother at 2pm.

title: Field guide entries: first batches
summary: Wren shared field notes and MIST drafted most of the entries for her Harlow Bay wetlands field guide: reedbed and pool plants, saltmarsh plants, birds such as curlew, redshank and marsh harrier, and the first insects and mammals, each with identification, local sites, season and a confusion species.

title: Field guide entries: last batch
summary: MIST drafted the remaining entries for the wetlands field guide, ending with the sedge warbler, and Wren saved all thirty to her field guide note.

title: Fixing the clicking bike
summary: Wren's bike clicked once per pedal stroke. The left pedal was loose, so MIST explained its reverse thread for tightening. For gears skipping on the biggest cog, a quarter turn of the rear barrel adjuster. The last service was in October, and a reminder was set to book one in April.
open_threads: book a bike service in April

title: February spending review
summary: Wren reviewed February spending: 1,940 pounds against a plan of 1,850, over on eating out and a one-off chainring. The heat pump savings pot is at 2,350 of 4,000, and she raised saving to 400 a month. Two unused subscriptions were flagged for cancelling.

title: Starting the conference talk
summary: Wren began her twenty-minute Westmere conference talk on the Lowmoor model: about twelve slides, rehearsals with Jonah as audience, opening with Felix's drone photo of the 2023 flood, and how to field hard questions. Abstracts are due 31 March; MIST drafted and saved the opening line.
open_threads: show Priya the outline on Thursday

title: Book club night and quitting pottery
summary: After book club, where everyone loved the ending of The Salt Road and April's pick is a memoir about lighthouse keepers, Wren said she had quit her pottery class and asked MIST to forget it, freeing Thursday evenings for talk rehearsals.

title: Packing the survey kit
summary: Wren packed for the Fenwick estuary survey item by item: waders, GPS, sediment corer, sample bags, cool box, ice packs, notebook, pencils, tide table, waterproof, head torch, first aid kit, batteries, drone batteries for Felix, lunch, flask, sun cream, hat, gloves and permits.

title: Reading back the survey kit list
summary: Wren asked to hear the full survey kit list back, and MIST read out all twenty items.

title: Jonah's garden bench
summary: Jonah has started his oak garden bench and is practising dovetails on offcuts. He wants it done before summer, so joints this month, assembly in April and oiling in May, with a hard wax oil so it does not go grey. Wren added a marking gauge to her gift ideas for his May birthday.

title: Imogen's training and a food correction
summary: Imogen ran 32 km in training for the Fellside ultra and asked Wren to crew for her. For dinner, Wren corrected a food dislike: it is fennel she cannot stand, not cilantro. They settled on fish tacos with cilantro and lime.

title: Stargazing and Biscuit's breed
summary: With clear skies, MIST suggested Jupiter and its four big moons and the Orion nebula for Wren's 90mm telescope. Wren corrected Biscuit's breed to basset hound, and MIST logged the session in her astronomy log.

title: Friday morning and a forgotten habit
summary: Wren turned on the hall lights, checked the drizzly weather, asked MIST to forget a personal habit, started the coffee machine, set a porridge timer and heard her first meeting: a 10:00 call with the Marrow Creek recruiter.

title: Accepting the Marrow Creek job
summary: Wren decided to accept the Marrow Creek job after talking it over with Jonah. MIST drafted a short resignation letter to Priya with a last day of 3 April, noted the start date of 6 April, suggested Felix take over the Lowmoor model and confirmed she can still give the Westmere talk.
open_threads: give Priya the letter on Monday

title: Switching energy supplier
summary: After a 12 percent price rise from Coastline Energy, Wren switched to Brightgrid, which Rafael recommended: a fixed tariff about 9 percent cheaper with a 60 pound exit fee and a heat pump night tariff. Her heat pump savings reached 2,750 of 4,000.

title: Estuary birding walk
summary: Wren saw her first marsh harrier of the year, about forty curlews and three little egrets on the estuary, and Biscuit lost an argument with a heron. MIST logged the sightings, suggested the Skerry Point lagoon for avocets in April and gave tomorrow's high water at 8:20.

title: Second Sunday batch cooking
summary: Wren prepped a roasted vegetable traybake, a pesto pasta salad without olives and overnight oats with oat milk, split into lunches and dinners, and set a 2pm reminder to call her mother.

title: Weekly review
summary: Wren reviewed her week: accepting the Marrow Creek job, switching energy supplier, finishing The Salt Road and starting the conference talk. She is eight books into thirty, cancelled two forgotten subscriptions, logged her knee at 2 out of 10 and looked ahead to handing in her resignation, the physio review and showing Priya the outline.

title: Looking ahead to April
summary: Wren looked ahead: Imogen visits 21 to 23 March, her Tidewater notice ends 3 April, the Marrow Creek job starts 6 April and the kayak rolling course on 11 April at the harbour pool. She needs a new wetsuit, collects the allotment keys on 1 April and blocked out the weekend of 4 and 5 April.
